macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks fall as oil prices surge
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.23% to 52,215.16, the S&P 500 declined 0.52% to 7,623.68, and the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.21% to 25,955.34. Rising oil prices, Middle East tensions and concerns about costly artificial-intelligence investment pressured sentiment.

items.title: Fed expected to hold rates next week
items.summary: Markets broadly expect the Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged at its upcoming meeting, while investors look for signals about the possibility of a December rate increase. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 5.0%.

items.title: Oil reaches five-month high amid Middle East concerns
items.summary: Oil prices climbed as markets assessed the risk of renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities and potential attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. The jump in energy costs added to inflation concerns and weighed on equities.

items.title: American Express to cut 5% of workforce
items.summary: American Express announced plans to reduce its global workforce by about 5% while raising its profit forecast. Its shares fell as the company cited preparations for increased artificial-intelligence adoption.

items.title: SLB beats profit expectations
items.summary: Oilfield-services company SLB reported third-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates, sending its shares up about 7% as higher oil prices supported the sector.

items.title: U.S. business activity remains strong but cost pressures persist
items.summary: October flash data showed U.S. services activity slowing modestly to 57.9 from 58.8, while manufacturing activity rose to a 53-month high of 56.0. Rising input costs remained a key concern.

items.title: Big technology earnings in focus
items.summary: About one-third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report results next week, including Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon. Investors are expected to scrutinize their artificial-intelligence capital-spending plans after a volatile week for technology stocks.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies retreat
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 1.2% to roughly $80,844 over 24 hours, while Ether declined 1.4% to about $2,379. The total crypto market capitalization dropped 1.1% to approximately $2.81 trillion, with Solana and XRP also losing ground.

items.title: Initia halts blockchain after $2.6 million exploit
items.summary: Initia suspended its layer-1 blockchain and associated rollups after an attacker reportedly exploited a flaw to mint tokens without authorization and cash out roughly $2.6 million. The project is assessing the incident with validators and exchanges.

items.title: U.S. stablecoin rules finalized under the GENIUS Act
items.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency finalized rules covering stablecoin reserves, redemptions, risk management, custody and issuer supervision. The rules are scheduled to take effect on January 18, 2027.

items.title: Solana activates Alpenglow mainnet upgrade
items.summary: Solana deployed its Alpenglow upgrade on mainnet, introducing the Votor consensus system and targeting approximately 150-millisecond transaction finality, compared with about 12.8 seconds under the previous TowerBFT system.

items.title: Crypto market liquidations accelerate
items.summary: Crypto markets recorded hundreds of millions of dollars in liquidations over the past 24 hours, predominantly affecting leveraged long positions. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs also saw approximately $635 million in net outflows in the latest reported session.

items.title: HSBC launches Hong Kong dollar stablecoin on PayMe
items.summary: HSBC launched RedCoin, a Hong Kong dollar-denominated stablecoin, through its PayMe app, giving the bank’s users access to a regulated digital-money product.

items.title: Ethereum Glamsterdam testnet activation postponed
items.summary: Ethereum developers postponed the planned Glamsterdam upgrade activation on the Hoodi test network after ChainSecurity identified potential gas-accounting problems that could cause valid operations to fail or contracts to receive unexpected gas costs.

items.title: Cysic bridge exploited and suspended
items.summary: Cysic suspended its cross-chain bridge after an unauthorized minting of approximately 10 million CYS tokens on BNB Smart Chain. Funds linked to the exploit were reportedly moved through Tornado Cash.

items.title: Switzerland approves first retail ETF holding bitcoin directly
items.summary: FINMA approved Switzerland’s first retail exchange-traded fund that invests directly in bitcoin, expanding regulated access to the asset for retail investors.

items.title: Dormant bitcoin wallet moves 411 BTC
items.summary: A bitcoin wallet that had been inactive since 2013 transferred 411 BTC, worth approximately $34 million at the time of reporting.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Moonshot AI launches Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.summary: Moonshot AI introduced Kimi K3.1 Pro, a large open-weight model with a 1-million-token context window, coding and 3D-modeling capabilities, and a faster Highspeed variant. The company says it removed cyber-related training data and plans to release the model weights on November 4.

items.title: Inception releases Mercury 3 diffusion language model
items.summary: Inception launched Mercury 3, a diffusion-based language model that reportedly generates up to 1,068 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs and supports a 1-million-token context window. It is available through the Inception API and several distribution platforms.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B
items.summary: NVIDIA released an open small language model designed for local voice assistants, game characters, and robots. The model targets systems with roughly 4 GB of VRAM, including RTX GPUs and Jetson devices.

items.title: Canva launches Craft image-generation model
items.summary: Canva introduced Craft, its first in-house image model, which generates images up to 2K resolution across 30 aspect ratios. The model is available in Canva’s Dream Lab and through the Canva API, with support for layered design workflows.

items.title: Recursive releases Flint laptop coding model
items.summary: Recursive released Flint, a coding model designed to run on a MacBook and reportedly built substantially with assistance from AI. The launch highlights growing interest in self-improving and locally deployable coding systems.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly advances major funding round
items.summary: OpenAI is reportedly nearing a funding round of approximately $30 billion at a valuation around $1.25 trillion, with Middle Eastern investors and Coatue among the potential participants. The financing discussions reportedly include expanded computing capacity.

items.title: Hugging Face releases Carbon-X DNA model
items.summary: Hugging Face released Carbon-X, an open AI model intended for conversational analysis of DNA. The model is positioned as a research tool and is not validated for medical decision-making.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: AI copycat games raise concerns across the industry
items.summary: Developers, particularly in South Korea, are reportedly canceling demos after AI-generated imitators appeared soon after promotional footage. Industry figures are calling for stronger protections against rapid cloning of game concepts and mechanics.

items.title: Sashi owner alleges preferential treatment in CS2 rules dispute
items.summary: Sashi’s owner accused Valve of giving preferential treatment to BC.Game in connection with Counter-Strike 2 regional roster rules. Sashi also parted ways with players TjP and Hatz.

items.title: Movistar KOI upset Bilibili Gaming at Worlds 2026
items.summary: Movistar KOI defeated fourth-ranked Bilibili Gaming 1–0 in the opening round of the League of Legends Worlds 2026 group stage.

items.title: Google and NODWIN announce Google Play Arena mobile esports series
items.summary: Google and NODWIN Gaming unveiled a six-game mobile esports competition in India featuring open qualifiers, with cricket star MS Dhoni involved in the initiative.

items.title: Riot extends 2XKO community event support through 2027
items.summary: Riot Games will continue its start.gg Community Events Support programme for 2XKO through the end of 2027, despite plans to end active development of the fighting game in late 2026.

items.title: Final Fantasy Resonance launches across major platforms
items.summary: Final Fantasy Resonance became available on PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch, and Nintendo Switch 2 on October 22, 2026.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 releases worldwide
items.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launched globally and has reportedly received positive player reactions, according to gaming coverage.

items.title: Liquid Swords reportedly shuts down after financial problems
items.summary: Swedish studio Liquid Swords, known for Samson, reportedly declared bankruptcy after months of unpaid wages; its company and assets are being offered for sale.

items.title: US bill proposes stronger digital game ownership rights
items.summary: Representative Ritchie Torres announced the Power To The Players Act, which would seek offline access requirements before server shutdowns and protections for resale of digital games.
